data.one_liner: Flutter plugin to open various native device settings screens on Android and iOS.
data.what_it_does: Provides a comprehensive set of methods to open specific native operating system settings screens, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Data Roaming, and Location Source on Android. On iOS, it defaults to opening the app settings screen.
use_when: You need to direct users to specific system settings screens from within your Android app
You want to prompt users to enable permissions or connections like Wi-Fi or Bluetooth
avoid_when: You need deep and reliable integration across many non-Android platforms, as iOS support is limited to opening app settings
You prefer handling permissions via declarative UI or in-app dialogs without leaving the app
strengths: Supports a massive range of individual settings screens on Android
Simple method-based API for quick invocation
weaknesses: iOS functionality is limited to opening the app settings page rather than specific setting panes
Relies on native intents that may change across Android OS versions
data.setup_notes: No special native configuration or permissions are strictly documented beyond standard plugin inclusion, though specific settings may require appropriate runtime permissions.

alternatives.name: app_settings
alternatives.why_pick_it: It serves a similar purpose of opening device settings screens and is available in the catalog.
